newsitem.title: USA: Rohm and Haas sees slower growth rate.
newsitem.headline: Rohm and Haas sees slower growth rate.

text.p: Rohm and Haas Co said Thursday it will find it hard to maintain during the second half of the year the same earnings growth rate that it enjoyed in the first half.

"Our performance in the first half gave us a fast start to the year," it said in a statement. "But it will be more challenging to report earnings growth at this rate for the rest of 1997." The company, which makes plastics, coatings and other chemicals, reported a profit of $3.47 a share for the first six months of the year, a 17-percent increase over the $2.96 per share reported for the same period a year ago.
"We expect to report earnings improvements in the third and fourth quarters of 1997, but at a slower pace than we have seen thus far," it said.

Rohm and Haas said unit volume growth accelerated strongly during the second half of 1996, which could affect 1997's remaining year-over-year comparisons. It also said foreign currencies continued to be a drag on 1997 earnings growth.
The company said it was confident that it would report its sixth consecutive year of earnings improvements in 1997, as long as world economies and raw material costs remained in a steady state.
